government.title: Social Norms, State Punishment, and Motivation Crowding in Anti‐Corruption Messaging: Experimental Evidence From China
government.short_title: Social Norms, State Punishment, and Motivation Crowding in Anti‐Corruption Messaging: Experime…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how people's beliefs about corruption influence their attitudes towards fighting it. In a large survey experiment conducted in China, researchers found that when people were told the actual level of tolerance for corruption is much lower than they thought, it made them more likely to want to fight corruption. However, if this information was paired with suggestions of punishment, it seemed to weaken the effect. This shows that simply telling people about how corrupt others are might not be as effective as also showing what actions can be taken against it.

government.title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Public Rights
government.short_title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Pu…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how governments in Iran handle situations where their actions harm collective interests or public rights. It examines legal systems that provide ways to compensate for such harms and restore balance. The research finds there are different types of compensation depending on whether the government acted wrongfully or not, and it also covers cases where they did something lawful but still caused damage. Challenges like unclear laws, difficulty proving harm in collective situations, and lack of coordination between different parts of the system can make these mechanisms less effective even if the basic rules are clear.

government.short_title: A Qualitative Analysis of Administrative Transparency Requirements in Government Construction…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how governments should make their construction contract processes more transparent to prevent inefficiencies and corruption. It covers all stages from deciding what to build to evaluating its success. Transparency isn't just about sharing information; it also means having clear rules, fair procedures, and being able to prove decisions were right. The court's rulings on this matter help enforce transparency as a legal requirement.

government.title: The Dual Impact of International Sanctions and FATF Requirements on the Independence and Effectiveness of Government Financial Supervision in Iran’s Public Law System
government.short_title: The Dual Impact of International Sanctions and FATF Requirements on the Independence and Effec…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: Financial supervision in Iran faces significant challenges due to both international sanctions and FATF requirements. These pressures affect how government institutions manage resources and ensure transparency. Sanctions limit access to data and cooperation with other countries, while FATF standards promote more formal procedures for oversight but also increase compliance costs. This creates a complex environment where institutions can gain technical tools but lose their independence due to external constraints like sanctions.

government.title: The Role of Government Structure in the Emergence of Crimes Against Humanity
government.short_title: The Role of Government Structure in the Emergence of Crimes Against Humanity
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: The study found that certain government structures can facilitate crimes against humanity by concentrating power in authoritarian regimes, allowing discriminatory ideologies to dominate, causing crises in legitimacy, or implementing unfair economic policies. These factors weaken checks on violence, legitimize harmful actions, suppress opposition groups, and cause harm to specific populations. To prevent such crimes, it's important for governments to strengthen the rule of law, ensure judicial independence, expand democratic oversight, and promote human rights values within their systems.

government.title: Evaluation of the Policymaking System and Institutions for Combating Administrative Corruption in Afghanistan during the Republican Period (2004–2021)
government.short_title: Evaluation of the Policymaking System and Institutions for Combating Administrative Corruption…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: During the Republican period in Afghanistan (2004-2021), administrative corruption was a major issue affecting governance. The government worked with international support to create laws, anti-corruption strategies, and institutions. However, despite progress in these areas, corruption did not significantly decrease. The study found that while there were improvements in legislation and institution building, the effectiveness of policies weakened at implementation stages.

government.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
government.short_title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Inte…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This research evaluates Iran's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to see how well it supports responsible use of AI. The strategy emphasizes values like human dignity and national priorities, but lacks clear plans for key areas like funding, data access, and regulation. To succeed, the strategy needs more specific details on these aspects. Practitioners should focus not just on ethical principles, but also on practical steps to ensure AI is used responsibly and effectively in Iran.

government.title: Challenges of Environmental Governance in Iraq and Strategies for Its Strengthening Based on Sustainable Development Standards
government.short_title: Challenges of Environmental Governance in Iraq and Strategies for Its Strengthening Based on S…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: Iraq faces significant challenges in managing its environment due to structural, legal, institutional, and security issues that harm public health, resources, and social stability. Despite having laws and international commitments, Iraq's environmental governance system is ineffective. To improve this, reforms are needed on multiple fronts including strengthening legislation, empowering institutions, integrating environmental concerns into economic policies, and enhancing regional and international cooperation. Aligning with sustainable development principles like good governance, stakeholder participation, and accountability can help address these issues and pave the way for Iraq's sustainable future.

government.title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Official Channels: A Critical Analysis of the 2013 Anti‑Smuggling Law and Its 2021 Amendments
government.short_title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Of…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: The smuggling of goods and currency through official channels in Iran remains a significant issue despite various laws enacted over the years. While there have been efforts like the 2013 Anti-Smuggling Law and subsequent amendments, this practice has not decreased but may have worsened in some areas such as reverse smuggling and organized currency trafficking. This article examines how well these laws balance different goals like prevention, repression, rehabilitation, and compensation. It found that while there are positive changes, the law still faces major issues including a broad definition of smuggling, multiple bodies leading to lengthy proceedings, disproportionate penalties, and weak enforcement due to corruption.

government.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
government.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
government.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
government.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

government.title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities of Nigeria
government.short_title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities…
government.plain_summary: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) was implemented in 2015 to centralize public funds and improve transparency and accountability in Nigerian federal universities, but financial irregularities still occur. This study found that TSA has improved transparency and accountability significantly (p=0.004), but also faces challenges like bureaucratic delays and actors circumventing the system. Corruption persists as it transforms into less traceable forms. Despite savings of over 10 trillion Naira nationally, corruption perception scores remain low.

government.title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary After Indonesian Constitutional Court Decision No. 66/PUU-XXIV/2026: A Fiqh Siyasah Perspective
government.short_title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary…
government.source: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review
government.plain_summary: This research looks at the difference between maladministration and corruption, using a specific case about buying Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia. It found four key factors to decide if something is corruption: whether someone intended to do wrong, if they got personal benefit from it, if money was lost as a result, and if proper steps were taken afterward. The study also suggests that when all these factors are met, what started as maladministration can be considered corruption. However, the research points out there should be an initial check by a special committee before going to criminal courts.

government.short_title: Interaction between the Investigator and the Operational Units of the Department for Economic…
government.plain_summary: When investigating reports of economic crimes, the key players involved are the inquiry officers and the units for economic security and anti-corruption (ESAC). Based on recent data showing a high number of detected crimes, it's important to follow written instructions from the inquiry officer. This includes coordinating plans, preserving evidence like documents and digital records, presenting findings clearly, and having prosecutorial oversight. A five-step model has been proposed for how these interactions should ideally occur.

government.title: Practical Aspects of Assessing Legal Norms for Corruption-Prone Provisions in the Conduct of Anti-Corruption Expertise
government.short_title: Practical Aspects of Assessing Legal Norms for Corruption-Prone Provisions in the Conduct of A…
government.plain_summary: This article talks about how to check if rules against corruption are good enough when state and local officials look at new laws. It explains how to do this check properly and gives examples from real life. The article also suggests ways to make sure these checks are better and faster, so new laws can be made with less chance of corruption. This is important for keeping things fair and stopping bad people from taking advantage.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.short_title: Utilization of State-Confiscated Property from Corruption Crimes Through Lease Agreements
government.plain_summary: State confiscated property, like items seized in court, can be managed by the government to maximize economic value. This property is usually sold through auctions. But if items don't sell, they need to be stored and secured, which can be costly. To solve this, Indonesia allows leasing these items.

government.title: State-level public corruption and taxpayer fraud
government.short_title: State-level public corruption and taxpayer fraud
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how corruption in state governments affects people's willingness to pay federal taxes. It found that states with more corruption also have higher rates of people being caught for not paying their taxes. This means that if state leaders are not honest, it might make people less likely to follow federal tax rules. Understanding this can help improve tax collection and ensure that governments have the money they need to function.

government.title: Real-Time Internal Control Dynamics and Fraud Prevention: A Framework for Strengthening Financial Integrity in Public Sectors
government.short_title: Real-Time Internal Control Dynamics and Fraud Prevention: A Framework for Strengthening Financ…
government.source: International Review of Management and Marketing
government.plain_summary: This study focuses on improving financial integrity in the Nigerian public sector by examining how real-time internal control practices can prevent fraud. It found that real-time authorisation significantly reduces unauthorized activities and enhances compliance. Periodic checks also help in detecting irregularities promptly. However, biometric authentication like fingerprint scanning and facial recognition did not show a clear benefit in this context.

government.title: The Concept of Anti-Corruption Propaganda
government.short_title: The Concept of Anti-Corruption Propaganda
government.plain_summary: This article explains different ways to talk about fighting corruption and breaks down what it means in simple terms. It looks at laws that deal with preventing corrupt practices and how they apply across regions. The piece also talks about how anti-corruption efforts fit into broader ideas about good governance. By examining these, the author creates a definition of anti-corruption propaganda that can be used by people who want to stop corruption in their work or organization.

government.title: Combating Corruption in the Migration Sector: The History and the Present Time
government.short_title: Combating Corruption in the Migration Sector: The History and the Present Time
government.plain_summary: Corruption is widespread in the migration sector, posing significant risks to national security and foreign policy. In Russia, there has been an increase in migration-related crimes, which exposes this area to corruption risks. To combat these issues, it's important to strengthen laws and regulations related to migration, ensuring they are effective against corruption. This can help protect citizens from exploitation and reduce the risk of international conflicts over migration policies.

government.title: The Role of Ethics in the Implementation of Anti-Corruption Standards for Civil Servants in Russia and China
government.short_title: The Role of Ethics in the Implementation of Anti-Corruption Standards for Civil Servants in Ru…
government.source: Public International and Private International Law
government.plain_summary: Corruption damages trust in government by civil servants. To fight it effectively, we need strong ethical standards alongside institutional changes. Russia and China have taken different approaches to this; studying their methods can help create better systems globally. Understanding both universal principles and cultural specifics is key for creating effective anti-corruption measures.

government.short_title: Crime Reporting and Analysis Through the Geographic Information System-Based Management: Enhan…
government.source: International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how using a Geographic Information System (GIS) can help police better fight illegal drug activities in a specific area of Oriental Mindoro. By gathering information about crimes and mapping them, the system helps officers plan their work more effectively. The study found that while some issues like lack of support from higher-ups are causing problems, the overall use of GIS is very good. To keep this working well, they need to provide better equipment for officers and make sure people's privacy is protected.

government.title: Working Paper 63: Anticipating future corruption
government.short_title: Working Paper 63: Anticipating future corruption
government.source: Basel Institute on Governance Working Papers
government.plain_summary: This working paper from the Basel Institute on Governance discusses how understanding corruption in complex systems can help improve anti-corruption efforts. It introduces foresight and anticipatory governance approaches to anticipate potential issues and opportunities before they happen, making strategies more effective against corruption. Practitioners can use these insights to develop proactive plans that are less reactive and better equipped to handle future challenges.

government.title: Digital Anti-Corruption Mechanisms in Uzbekistan: Legal Frameworks, E-Government Tools, and Reform Challenges
government.short_title: Digital Anti-Corruption Mechanisms in Uzbekistan: Legal Frameworks, E-Government Tools, and Re…
government.source: Uzbek Journal of Law and Digital Policy
government.plain_summary: Uzbekistan has been strengthening its fight against corruption by integrating digital tools into its legal framework. They have passed laws like the 2017 "Law on Combating Corruption" and declared a state of emergency in December 2025 to address ongoing issues. The country also launched a Digital Compliance system in July 2026, which has improved e-government transparency and efficiency. However, challenges remain such as ensuring institutional independence, cybersecurity threats, and the risk that digital controls might not be as effective as traditional methods of oversight.

government.title: Implementation of the Integrity Zone Development Policy toward a Corruption-Free Area at Statistics Indonesia (BPS) Cianjur Regency
government.short_title: Implementation of the Integrity Zone Development Policy toward a Corruption-Free Area at Stati…
government.source: International Journal of Economics, Management and Accounting (IJEMA)
government.plain_summary: The Corruption-Free Area policy at Statistics Indonesia's Cianjur Regency office aims to create a corruption-free environment by implementing an integrity zone development strategy. This study used a descriptive qualitative approach based on George C. Edwards III’s model, which includes communication, resources, disposition, and bureaucratic structure. While the employees have implemented these four variables, the effectiveness is not yet fully achieved.

government.title: Black Magic and Anti-Superstition Laws in India: A Critical Analysis of Criminal Liability, Constitutional Rights and Protection of Victims
government.short_title: Black Magic and Anti-Superstition Laws in India: A Critical Analysis of Criminal Liability, Co…
government.source: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
government.plain_summary: In India, practices like black magic can lead to various abuses such as fraud, violence, abuse, and even death. While people's beliefs are not illegal, exploiting these beliefs for harm is. Currently, there isn't a single comprehensive law covering all of this. Instead, different laws address specific issues like witchcraft or fraudulent advertisements.

government.title: Legal Corruption in the Government: An Experimental Study on the Role of Civil Servants' Political Ideology
government.short_title: Legal Corruption in the Government: An Experimental Study on the Role of Civil Servants' Polit…
government.plain_summary: This research examines how civil servants view government legal corruption using a survey experiment involving over 2000 South Korean civil servants. It found that their judgment of legal corruption is influenced by their own political ideology. Civil servants are more critical when the government they work for has different political views from theirs, compared to when it aligns with them. This study highlights how political beliefs shape perceptions of corruption within public institutions, suggesting that understanding these ideological differences can help in addressing and preventing corruption effectively.

government.title: ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICIES AND DEMOCRATIC GOVERNANCE IN NIGERIA: AN EVALUATION OF THE INDEPENDENT CORRUPT PRACTICES AND OTHER RELATED OFFENCES COMMISSION (ICPC)
government.short_title: ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICIES AND DEMOCRATIC GOVERNANCE IN NIGERIA: AN EVALUATION OF THE INDEPENDEN…
government.source: International Journal of Business, Management, Behavioral Research and Innovations
government.plain_summary: Corruption is a significant issue in Nigeria that affects democratic governance and public administration. Despite having an anti-corruption body called the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offenses Commission (ICPC), corruption continues to be prevalent. The ICPC has implemented various measures like prevention programs, audits of government departments, public education campaigns, asset recovery, and prosecuting offenders. However, challenges such as lack of funding, political interference, judicial delays, weak collaboration among agencies, and low conviction rates limit its effectiveness.

government.title: Determinants and Impact of Corruption on Public Service Delivery in Lafia Local Government Council, Nasarawa State, Nigeria
government.short_title: Determinants and Impact of Corruption on Public Service Delivery in Lafia Local Government Cou…
government.source: JOURNAL OF POLITICAL SCIENCE AND LEADERSHIP RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how corruption affects service delivery in Lafia, a local government area in Nigeria. It found that factors like lack of transparency, weak institutions, political interference, low salaries, and poor enforcement of anti-corruption laws lead to high levels of corruption. Corruption causes delays in projects, uses cheap materials, stops projects from starting, increases the cost of services, and makes it harder for people who don't have power to get help. To fix this, the government should improve how they run things by being more open about their spending and making sure anti-corruption laws are followed.

government.title: Evaluating Public Service Innovation Using Digital Transformation, Transparency, and Citizen Satisfaction Across Government Administrative Institutions
government.short_title: Evaluating Public Service Innovation Using Digital Transformation, Transparency, and Citizen S…
government.source: Mandalika Journal of Business and Management Studies
government.plain_summary: This study evaluates how governments can improve their services using digital tools, being more open with information, and ensuring citizens are happy with what they get from the government. It found that making services easier to access online, sharing more information about how decisions are made, and regularly checking if people like getting service helps a lot in improving trust and efficiency of government work. The study suggests using these three areas - digital tools, transparency, and citizen satisfaction - as key measures for assessing how well public services meet the needs of citizens. This can help governments understand what works best to make their services better.

government.title: Evaluation of the Impact of Corruption on Administrative System in Mubi North Local Government Council of Adamawa State
government.short_title: Evaluation of the Impact of Corruption on Administrative System in Mubi North Local Government…
government.source: JOURNAL OF POLITICAL SCIENCE AND LEADERSHIP RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how corruption affects a local government council in Adamawa State called Mubi North. It found that corruption causes problems like people not trusting the council or getting needed services. The study also showed that weak rules and poor management contribute to corruption. To fix this, the council needs better oversight, fairer pay for workers, and stronger anti-corruption laws.

government.short_title: Anti-Corruption Mitigatory Measures in Trading of Maize Grain and Tobacco: A Critical Analysis…
government.source: JOURNAL OF HUMANITIES AND SOCIAL POLICY
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how corruption affects the trading of maize grain and tobacco in Zimbabwe. It found issues like farmers not getting paid properly or having their grain handled improperly by Grain Marketing Boards. The study also noted problems with smuggled grain entering the country for resale. To fix these issues, it suggests ways to prevent corruption based on earlier research.

government.title: Comparative Analysis of Anti-Corruption Laws and Governance Mechanisms in Developing Countries
government.short_title: Comparative Analysis of Anti-Corruption Laws and Governance Mechanisms in Developing Countries
government.source: European Journal of Law, Interdisciplinary Legal Ethics and Jurisprudence Governance Practices
government.plain_summary: Corruption is a major issue in developing countries affecting everything from economic growth to social justice. Many governments have created laws and systems to fight corruption like anti-corruption commissions, whistleblower protection laws, and digital initiatives. However, these efforts are not always successful due to factors like political commitment and local conditions. Comparing how different countries handle corruption can help identify what works best.

government.title: Why Disclosure Regimes Fail to Produce Accountability: A Theory of Transparency Architecture
government.short_title: Why Disclosure Regimes Fail to Produce Accountability: A Theory of Transparency Architecture
government.plain_summary: This study examines why strict rules requiring organizations to disclose more information don't necessarily lead to better oversight. It found that simply making more disclosures doesn’t automatically improve how people understand and use this information. The problem is that current methods for measuring transparency focus too much on the quantity of disclosures, without considering how detailed or useful these disclosures are. This leads to situations where organizations comply with disclosure rules but still provide insufficiently informative data.

government.title: Why Comply? Explaining Sectoral Patterns in GRECO 'S Anti‐Corruption Recommendations
government.short_title: Why Comply? Explaining Sectoral Patterns in GRECO 'S Anti‐Corruption Recommendations
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how different parts of governments in various countries follow recommendations aimed at fighting corruption. It found that prosecutors are followed most closely, judges second, but members of parliament least. The reasons why vary based on the costs these groups face for changing their ways compared to their influence over changes being made. This research suggests focusing more on specific sectors can help improve anti-corruption efforts rather than just looking at countries as a whole.

government.title: POLITICAL CORRUPTION AND ITS IMPACT ON PUBLIC GOVERNANCE IN POST-APARTHEID SOUTH AFRICA
government.short_title: POLITICAL CORRUPTION AND ITS IMPACT ON PUBLIC GOVERNANCE IN POST-APARTHEID SOUTH AFRICA
government.source: Ayika – Journal of Environment and Politics in Africa
government.plain_summary: Political corruption continues to be a major issue in South Africa's governance, affecting various aspects like service delivery, economic growth, and trust in institutions. Despite efforts, the government faces challenges in controlling corruption, especially in areas like public procurement. Understanding these impacts is crucial for improving governance and ensuring that resources are used effectively to benefit citizens. Future research should evaluate what measures work best to reduce political corruption.

government.title: AI-DRIVEN WORKFORCE OPTIMIZATION IN E-BANKING: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN TAMIL NADU’S PUBLIC SECTOR BANKS
government.short_title: AI-DRIVEN WORKFORCE OPTIMIZATION IN E-BANKING: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN TAMIL NADU’S PU…
government.source: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
government.plain_summary: The shift towards e-banking has transformed how public sector banks operate and serve customers, improving service delivery but also creating challenges like workforce flexibility issues and digital skill gaps. Current methods often don't integrate performance measurement with digital transition plans effectively. To address these, a new AI-driven framework is proposed to optimize the workforce for e-banking in Tamil Nadu's public sector banks. This framework uses data analysis techniques such as machine learning models and sentiment analysis to predict employee readiness and needs, providing personalized training paths and strategic feedback.

government.title: “We would be foolish not to use influencers” – trading off public values in public-sector communication
government.short_title: “We would be foolish not to use influencers” – trading off public values in public-sector comm…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how government agencies work with social media influencers. It found that using influencers can help reach more people quickly but also raises concerns about transparency and accountability. To handle this, governments create rules for choosing influencers and ways to keep their messages consistent. These practices don't solve all the problems, but they try to manage them so the government's message stays true while still engaging with its audience effectively.

government.title: A framework for AI readiness and strategic adoption: developing a public sector AI maturity model through systematic review and synthesis
government.short_title: A framework for AI readiness and strategic adoption: developing a public sector AI maturity mo…

government.plain_summary: This study aims to help public sector organizations understand and adopt artificial intelligence effectively. It found that factors like leadership, governance, transparency, and ethical oversight are crucial for successful AI use in government. The research proposes a five-level maturity model showing how an organization can progress from using AI sporadically to integrating it into daily operations in a responsible way. This framework helps public sector leaders plan their AI journey systematically.

government.title: Structured prioritization of stakeholder preferences in digital governance: a comparative AHP framework for public-sector decision alignment
government.short_title: Structured prioritization of stakeholder preferences in digital governance: a comparative AHP…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how to better align digital governance decisions by understanding what different stakeholders value. It uses a framework called AHP, which helps identify the most important goals for improving things like quality of life, sustainability, innovation, and competitiveness in cities. By comparing these priorities across various groups, including public officials and citizens, we can see where there might be disagreements or gaps in how policies are made. This model allows city planners to make decisions that better reflect what people want and expect from their government.

nonprofit.title: The New Middle Class of Iran and the Demand for Reforming Domestic and Foreign Political Relations
nonprofit.short_title: The New Middle Class of Iran and the Demand for Reforming Domestic and Foreign Political Relat…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: The new middle class in Iran grew significantly after the Islamic Revolution and played a key role in pushing for reforms in both domestic and foreign policies. This group became more active in elections over time, aiming to influence how the government handled these areas. Despite their efforts through voting, they haven't been able to fully change the system's approach to politics internationally or domestically. Their success was mainly seen in getting more people involved in electoral processes.

nonprofit.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
nonprofit.short_title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Inte…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research evaluates Iran's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to see how well it supports responsible use of AI. The strategy emphasizes values like human dignity and national priorities, but lacks clear plans for key areas like funding, data access, and regulation. To succeed, the strategy needs more specific details on these aspects. Practitioners should focus not just on ethical principles, but also on practical steps to ensure AI is used responsibly and effectively in Iran.

nonprofit.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
nonprofit.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
nonprofit.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
nonprofit.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

nonprofit.title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary After Indonesian Constitutional Court Decision No. 66/PUU-XXIV/2026: A Fiqh Siyasah Perspective
nonprofit.short_title: Where Does Maladministration End and Corruption Begin? Delineating the Constitutional Boundary…
nonprofit.source: JISRev: Journal of Islamic Studies Review
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research looks at the difference between maladministration and corruption, using a specific case about buying Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia. It found four key factors to decide if something is corruption: whether someone intended to do wrong, if they got personal benefit from it, if money was lost as a result, and if proper steps were taken afterward. The study also suggests that when all these factors are met, what started as maladministration can be considered corruption. However, the research points out there should be an initial check by a special committee before going to criminal courts.

nonprofit.title: ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICIES AND DEMOCRATIC GOVERNANCE IN NIGERIA: AN EVALUATION OF THE INDEPENDENT CORRUPT PRACTICES AND OTHER RELATED OFFENCES COMMISSION (ICPC)
nonprofit.short_title: ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICIES AND DEMOCRATIC GOVERNANCE IN NIGERIA: AN EVALUATION OF THE INDEPENDEN…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Business, Management, Behavioral Research and Innovations
nonprofit.plain_summary: Corruption is a significant issue in Nigeria that affects democratic governance and public administration. Despite having an anti-corruption body called the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offenses Commission (ICPC), corruption continues to be prevalent. The ICPC has implemented various measures like prevention programs, audits of government departments, public education campaigns, asset recovery, and prosecuting offenders. However, challenges such as lack of funding, political interference, judicial delays, weak collaboration among agencies, and low conviction rates limit its effectiveness.

nonprofit.title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
nonprofit.short_title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
nonprofit.source: Journal of Social Politics and Governance (JSPG)
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.
